correctness.rationale: Uniform labels across steps and walkers give an exact classwise independent coupon-occupancy law. Classical geometric convolution is log-concave and yields strict log-concavity of the cumulative coupon completion law by a termwise ratio inequality. Telescoping floor differences balance every circular window, proving all-horizon stochastic order; eventual strictness proves necessity. Missing-coupon factorial moments yield Poisson limits with the displayed phase offsets, and Jensen yields the sharp penalty and equality cases. The unequal-size obstruction was exhaustively tabulated. The standalone program passed 190,907 finite exact assertions and directly enumerated actual walks, but the general result rests on the analytic steps.

value.rationale: The theorem solves the natural class-allocation optimization for parallel searchers in a periodic strongly connected directed graph, in the strong stochastic order for all horizons and parameters rather than optimizing an arbitrary slice or a mean only. It characterizes every optimal allocation, exposes a nonvanishing macroscopic start imbalance penalty in a sharp walker-density window, and identifies explicit unequal-size data where such a universal order fails. These provide interpretable structural and asymptotic information for stochastic parallel coverage.
